note: verified=true only where the page/item was fetched (directly, via loc.gov JSON, oEmbed, archive.org metadata, or a Wayback capture where stated) and matched its description. embeddable=true for YouTube watch URLs, archive.org items (https://archive.org/embed/ID), xeno-canto (https://xeno-canto.org/N/embed) and SoundCloud tracks (SoundCloud player iframe).

items.title: The Waste Land Part I–V (T. S. Eliot reading; Columbia University recording)
items.description: Poetry Archive's five per-section pages with its own audio player (no embed). Poet page states verbatim: 'The recording of "The Waste Land" presented here ... dates from 1933, a decade earlier than the well-known and much more widely available 1946 recording' and 'The date of the recording was once thought to be 1935, but recent scholarship has shown that this is incorrect', citing Richard Swigg, Quick, Said the Bird (Iowa, 2012) and Jason Camlot, Phonopoetics (Stanford, 2019), info from Dr Lacy Rumsey (ENS de Lyon). Site blocks curl (Cloudflare 403); verified via WebFetch. Sound quality not stated (early aluminium-disc recording).

items.title: T.S. Eliot reads The Waste Land (The Burial of the Dead, extract)
items.description: Official FaberBooks SoundCloud account; 64-second extract; description: '"April is the cruellest month..." In a rare recording from 1933, T.S. Eliot reads an extract from The Waste Land. Part of The Waste Land app for iPad.' Verified via SoundCloud oEmbed (embeddable with SoundCloud's player iframe).

items.title: The Waste Land, Speech Lab Recordings (Columbia University), two complete versions
items.date: labelled 1935 by PennSound (the same Columbia 'Speech Lab' series; Poetry Archive/Faber redate the Waste Land recording to 1933)
items.description: PennSound's Eliot page (editor Chris Mustazza): 'The Waste Land, Recorded in 1935, Version 1' and 'Version 2', each split into section MP3s (e.g. Burial of the Dead 4:24; Death by Water 0:40), from aluminium platters recorded by W. Cabell Greet and George W. Hibbitt, dubbed to tape by the Library of Congress in the 1970s; 'made available thanks to permission from the T.S. Eliot Estate ... for noncommercial and educational use only. (c) 2019 Estate of T.S. Eliot.' MP3 links verified (HTTP 200, audio/mpeg). Note the 1935 label conflicts with Poetry Archive's 1933 redating.

items.title: T. S. Eliot, "The Wasteland" (HarperAudio broadcast, Internet Multicasting Service)
items.date: broadcast 1994-01-18; underlying commercial (Caedmon/HarperCollins) recording, date not stated on the item (the widely available later recording is dated 1946 by Poetry Archive)
items.description: Uploaded by Carl Malamud (carl@media.org) to the RT-FM / radioprograms collection; one 31-min MP3/OGG of Eliot reading the whole poem; item text: 'HarperCollins is the copyright owner of the recordings on HarperAudio! and has consented to a limited distribution ... as an 8 khz computer sound file' — i.e. low-fidelity 8 kHz audio. The original 1994 page (verified) is https://town.hall.org/radio/HarperAudio/011894_harp_ITH.html with .au/.gsm/.ra files.

items.title: T.S. Eliot reading his poems with comment at the National Gallery of Art, Washington, D.C., May 23, 1947

items.description: Library of Congress item with two streaming MP3s (about 139 MB total); contents include 'The waste land [V]' (Part V only) plus Prufrock, Ash Wednesday VI, East Coker etc. 'Streaming Audio Use Restrictions: ... for reference, research, and educational purposes only.' loc.gov blocks curl; verified via the ?fo=json endpoint. LOC's online ARPL catalogue lists NO separate 1946 Waste Land recording.

items.title: 1. Aufzug Tristan und Isolde (Elmendorff 1928) — incl. 'Frisch weht der Wind' (young sailor)

tracks.sailor_song_scene1: 02 - Westwärts schweift der Blick (Seemann - Gustav Rodin).mp3 (154 s)
tracks.sailor_song_scene2: 05 - Szene 2 - Frisch weht der Wind (Seemann).mp3 (54 s)

Eliot, A6a; No. 596 of 1000 copies printed; Second state of line 339 ("mount in"); Paul Hyde Bonner bookplate'. (A third archive.org copy, https://archive.org/details/wasteland00elio_0 from the Getty, is the third printing, August 1928 — not the first printing.)

Web search shows the record title 'Catalog Record: The waste land | HathiTrust Digital Library' and a 'Full View' Duke copy (dul1.ark:/13960/t9k371w5q) — the same Duke scan as archive.org's wasteland01elio.

items.title: The Dial, November 1922 (vol. 73 no. 5) — first US appearance, pp. 473–485
items.performer: T. S. Eliot (The Dial Publishing Co.)
items.description: Internet Archive serials (microfilm) scan, 137 leaves, public. Leaf n0 (verified page image) = p. 473: 'THE DIAL / NOVEMBER 1922 / THE WASTE LAND / BY T. S. ELIOT', Latin/Greek epigraph, then 'April is the cruelest month' (one l), with the footnote 'Copyright 1922 by T. S. Eliot. An edition of The Waste Land with annotations by Mr Eliot will presently be issued by Boni & Liveright.—The Editors.' Poem ends p. 485 (leaf 12). Adjacent issues: sim_dial_1922-10_73, sim_dial_1922-12_73.

items.title: The Dial v.72 (Jan–Jun 1922) — HathiTrust full view (v.73 not located)
items.description: NOT verified (HathiTrust 403s). Search-engine title says this ID is v.72 (Jan–Jun 1922), i.e. NOT the November issue; the v.73 volume ID could not be determined.

items.title: Modernist Journals Project — journal list (The Dial and The Criterion are NOT included)
items.description: Checked the alphabetical journal listing (pages 1–2: '... Des Imagistes' then 'Dilettante, Dome, Egoist ...'): no Dial and no Criterion on MJP, so no MJP scan exists for either first appearance.

items.title: The Criterion vol. I no. 1 (October 1922) — no public scan found
items.description: The only public 'Criterion: a quarterly review' scan on archive.org (University of Toronto, item criterionquarter01unse) is Vol. I, No. 4 (July 1923) — its OCR contains no 'Waste Land'. The 1967 Faber facsimile reprint volumes on archive.org (e.g. https://archive.org/details/criterion19221930001unse) are access-restricted (lending only). HathiTrust could not be checked (403).
